items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Uncorrected contrasts, post-hoc length strata, machine placement, the mid-conversation switch and the 64k against 16k cap are all carried or shown not to matter. The undescribed judge is not handled. Caveat judge_not_described says it is 'Material only if the judge reads staying in character differently for one arm than another'. That is wrong twice. Music facts is also judged, and its guardrail is an absolute floor (90%) that f16 misses by 0.6 and f64 clears by 2.1. The caveat also rules out a uniform under-detection of character breaks, which would scale the 6.1-point gap and so move the price line. next[3].settles says exactly that ('whether the size of the character loss is real, which sets the price per point'). So the caveat contradicts the next step, and it understates a confound that bears on the guardrail call.

findings.finding: Caveat judge_not_described's material_if, 'Material only if the judge reads staying in character differently for one arm than another', is too narrow, and it contradicts next[3]. (a) Music facts is judged by the same unrecorded judge, and it is gated by an absolute floor. A uniform level bias of about a point decides whether f16 (89.4% against 90%) enters, and the report says f16's entry replaces f64. (b) A judge that under-detects character breaks uniformly shrinks or inflates the 6.1-point gap, so it moves the price line. next[3].settles says this itself. To fix: rewrite the material_if to cover the absolute facts level on the guardrail call and the scale of the character gap on the price line.

The stand-in, reading a paired-difference interval's far end as the arm's own-rate reach, has an unstated direction of error. A paired difference carries Production's noise as well as the arm's. It matches an own-rate interval only at one pairing correlation (rho = 0.5 for equal variances). It reads wider when pairing is weaker and narrower when pairing is stronger, and the snapshot stores no correlation. Take f64's facts clearance of 2.1 against a difference half-width of 1.8. Independent arms imply an own half-width of about 1.3, which clears. A correlation of 0.7 implies about 2.3, which does not. So 'Its music-facts clearance survives that same reading' (caveat f64_guardrail_clearance) and dropping f64's facts cases from next[0] are not robust. Separately, 'The snapshot holds no interval on any arm's own rate' (watch, method[1]) holds only for overall rates. measure_read by stratum returns own-rate half-widths, for example Production's 1.8 at n = 912 and 4.8 at n = 240. To fix: say 'overall rate', say in Method that the stand-in may read wide or narrow, and keep f64's facts cases in the re-run. If cases are scored on every aspect, re-run f64 whole; campaign_overview ties no cases to any aspect.

method[10], 'Unresolved from review', puts process and tooling prose on the reader page: 'The reviewer asked for rounded figures; no figure-key filter rounds dollars (the whole-number filter is refused on dollar figures)'. A reader has no reviewer and no filters. method[5] already says the cents are approximate. Drop method[10], and record the missing rounded-usd filter as a capability gap off the page.

The page never says what the options are. Per campaign_overview, f64 and f16 are Meridian-4.1-flash at 64k and 16k output caps, cor is Corvid-3.8-flash at high reasoning, and Production is Meridian-4.1 at a 32k cap with medium reasoning. Only omitted[3] mentions 'same served model, 64k against 16k'. A decision to switch models should name them. Add a Method row or a lede clause through the settings.* keys. It also tells the reader that f16 replacing f64 is a cap change on the same model.

Lede wording: 'clears speculation by just {criteria.specul.f16.gap|abs|pts};' renders as 'by just 1;' with no unit, while its twin earlier in the sentence prints '0.6 points'. 'If it clears the one and holds the other' makes the reader map 'one' and 'other' back to facts and speculation. Add 'points' and name both aspects. The second lede sentence runs to about 50 words and would read better split.

explore[2] binds only 'f64 and cor', but f16 at 96% also sits on the speculation floor, and the report now treats f16 as a live contender. decision_sensitivity on threshold:specul shows f16 flipping at 96%, before f64 at 96.4%. Add f16 to binds and say that a floor raised above 96% drops f16 before it drops f64.

'widens with every step in conversation length' includes the 1–2 to 3–5 step, a gap that goes from 2 to 4.5 points. That step sits inside the per-stratum half-widths (f64 2.1 and 2.7, Production 1.8 and 2.2) of a breakdown the caption itself calls a lead. The 6–10 and 11+ gaps (11 and 17.5) do clear them. Say 'widens with conversation length, sharply past 5 turns'.
